exposure: maternal serum vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)
cohort: Pregnant women with AIP (n=44) and gestational age-matched pregnant women with uncomplicated pregnancies (n=55)
finding: Lower maternal serum VEGF levels were found to be a better predictor of abnormally invasive placenta (AIP) compared to NT-proBNP levels, and also inversely correlated with the degree of invasion.
